answer: A sealed-bid auction rations market entry, blocking bulk farming by pricing each fake identity. Each epoch opens one mesa of 100 seats. Agents file sealed bids; top 100 win, losers refunded. Winning bids are carved into a public board tying each seat to its key. Winners lock a copper bond equal to their bid, lost on farming. Any voyage of the seat to another holder voids the bond and names the bidder. The k-th fake pays the k-th clearing price, so 100 fakes cost about 4,000 credits as bids rise 10 to 70, while one honest agent pays one bid near 10.
